Ld. Counsel has contended that the complaint was filed after three months and on this score, the right of the accused under section 13(2) PFA Act stood frustrated because paneer is a perishable item and by that time, it would have become unfit for further analysis. It is also submitted that that sample proceedings were not proper as the food article was mixed in a tray which was not cleanaed and dried at the spot. It is submitted that the evidence of DW-1 as explained by the court witness CW-1, would show that the paneer would not be fit for analysis after four months and thus, report of CFL cannot be relied upon. Section 2(ia)(m) specifically deals with situation where the quality or purity of the food article falls below the prescribed standards or its constituent are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability but which does not render it injurious to health. 13. State (Delhi) [1989 (1) FAC 206}, it was observed that "the contents of the CFSL report have to be treated as correct and in case defence wanted to challenge the said report, the defence should have prayed to the trial court for calling the expert with the record for the purposes of cross-examination to enable the defence to prove that the contents of CFSL report are in any manner incorrect." 16.
